items.title: Piper Sandler Names Top Industrial Software Stocks Amid Market Shift
items.summary: Investing.com -- Piper Sandler has transferred coverage of three industrial software companies with Overweight ratings, identifying them as high-quality assets positioned to withstand current market challenges. The firm notes a bifurcation in the software market between winners and losers, with these companies offering mission-critical workflows, domain expertise, and proprietary data that provide relative insulation from disruption.

items.title: Autodesk (ADSK) Stock May Be 39% Undervalued Despite New Agentic AI Push
items.summary: Autodesk shares have come under pressure over the past year, which puts fresh focus on a simple question for investors who care about fundamentals. Is the current valuation supported by the cash flows this software group is expected to generate. The stock has fallen 35.1% over the past 12 months, which puts the spotlight on whether that price now lines up with the cash the business can produce over time. Autodesk is pushing agentic AI deeper into its Forma, Fusion and Flow cloud platforms...

items.title: Autodesk (ADSK) Previewed A Cross Product Agentic AI Assistant
items.summary: Autodesk (NasdaqGS:ADSK) previewed a next-generation agentic AI experience across its key industry clouds, expanding beyond single-product use. The Autodesk Assistant AI platform is being extended to support cross-product workflows and future standalone access for users. Management also outlined plans to support third-party AI agents and signalled further Assistant-related developments targeted for 2027. items.title: What Could Send Autodesk Stock Higher?
items.summary: Autodesk (ADSK) has one fast-growing business in an industry that still uses little technology. That matters because the stock has fallen. Autodesk shares lost 33% over the past year as of September 23, 2026, while the S&P 500 returned 13%. A business like that could change how investors value the whole company. So which business is it, and is there proof it is working.

items.title: Adobe Stock Slides 18%: Value Play or Falling Knife?
items.summary: Adobe (ADBE) stock has fallen about 18% from its August 31 high, and the question is whether to buy. Its own trading history warrants caution: after past sharp drops, the stock was higher a year later only half the time. And Adobe is trading some near-term recurring-revenue growth for free users, a bet management says will play out over 2027.
